# Rust

Loaded when a Rust file is read. Not resident.

Load `prometheus-rust-workspace` before Rust implementation, review, refactoring, or
architecture work. It routes installed skills and owns Cargo timing; skill activation
does not authorize immediate command execution.

Use `rust-best-practices` generally, `rust-async-patterns` for async/concurrency, and
`rust-mcp-server-generator` for MCP work. Project dependency and protocol pins win.

## Phase-gated verification

- Batch related edits and use static reasoning or rust-analyzer during a phase.
- Run one consolidated Cargo validation batch only after a meaningful set of
  production functionality is complete at a change or phase boundary. An immediate,
  narrowly targeted compiler check is allowed only when compiler feedback is
  necessary to unblock implementation or the user requests it.
- Start with the smallest integration target that exercises the completed production
  path and real collaborators. Unit tests, module-local tests, and filtered function
  tests do not count as completion evidence. Escalate only when the change or failure
  crosses package boundaries.
- Reserve broad, release, cross-compile, feature-matrix, Miri, fuzzing, coverage,
  benchmark, and documentation commands for a final boundary or explicit request.
- After a failure, read all diagnostics, batch fixes, and rerun only the smallest
  integration command that confirms the completed behavior. Do not rerun after each
  edit.
- Run formatting once at a coherent phase boundary and avoid unrelated churn.
- Report commands, results, intentional deferrals, and any remaining integration gate.

## Hard rules

- Never `--release` during implementation; never cross-compile before the affected package gate passes.
- Use one build profile; use `--all-features` only when the project supports it or the user requests it.
- Never `panic = "abort"` on a profile that ships through `flutter_rust_bridge` — it needs unwinding.

## Build concurrency (A-10, G-4)

Within one workspace or target directory, serialize every Cargo command. Before an
expensive command, account for any Cargo process already running; if Cargo reports
lock contention, wait for or identify that process instead of starting retries.
Across isolated worktrees, keep the default separate target directories and a shared
`CARGO_HOME`; do not create extra target directories merely to bypass an ordinary
lock. Serialize dependency-mutating commands such as `cargo fetch`, `update`, and
`add` across worktrees. Never run `cargo clean` unless cleanup is the requested task.

## Structure — feature-based, inside Rust too

- **A bounded context is a crate.** Anything that must never be violated becomes a crate boundary, because
  the dependency graph is the only enforcement Rust gives for free. A domain crate is pure; nothing with
  I/O may become its dependency to silence a trait or borrow error.
- A library crate is organised by capability, never by technical kind: `orders/`, `pricing/`,
  `inventory/` — not `models.rs`, `utils.rs`, `helpers.rs`.
- A service crate: `src/features/<feature>/{domain,application,infrastructure,interface}`, plus
  `src/core/` (config, error, session) and `src/shared/`.
  `interface → application → domain ← infrastructure`. `domain` imports no axum, reqwest, sqlx, tokio or
  serde_json I/O. `interface` holds handlers and DTOs only. Features never import each other; shared code
  moves to `core/` or `shared/`.
- `mod.rs` files re-export and wire; they hold no logic.

## File size

No `.rs` file over 500 lines. Before it gets there, turn `foo.rs` into `foo/{mod.rs,…}` split by
responsibility (types, operations, errors), keeping the public path stable through re-exports.
`clippy::too_many_lines` covers functions.

## This repo — Rust is scaffolding, never a host dependency

- MCP servers are **STDIO only**: `rmcp` with `transport-io`. No Axum, no ports. Logs go to **stderr**;
  stdout is the protocol channel.
- No `nix`, no direct `libc`, no unix sockets, no `sh -c`. `std::env::temp_dir()`, never `/tmp`; the
  `dirs` crate, never `$HOME`. Target `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` must build.
- Never make `sccache` or any other wrapper mandatory. On a 16 GB machine: `cargo build -j 4`, and keep
  `lto` / `codegen-units = 1` in the release profile only.
